newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 6.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.

- Details of allegations of payments of more than one million Irish pounds from Dunnes Stores supermarket chain to a senior figure in the Fianna Fail political party are contained in formal correspondence between Ben Dunne and the rest of the Dunne family.
- Ireland's Criminal Assets Bureau has moved on one of the largest criminal gangs in the state, seizing documents and other materials in raids on nine houses in Dublin.
- Multi-party peace talks in Northern Ireland have been adjourned until June 3.

- The Irish cabinet will shortly consider a proposal to establish a new national manpower service as part of a drive to get more unemployed people back to work. The proposal is a central element of the new White Paper on Human Resource Development.
- A series of swoops led by Ireland's Criminal Assets Bureau was staged against a man alleged to be one of gangland's most notorious crime bosses.
- A major shake-up in the primary school curriculum for almost 500,000 pupils is proposed in a series of draft reports which signal basic revisions in what they are taught.

- A new National Employment Service Board (NESB) to oversee the Irish government's employment and training programmes is proposed in the draft White Paper on Human Resources Development, which is expected to come before the cabinet this month.

- Ireland's industrial development board, IDA, is focusing on wealthy German family-owned consumer goods and engineering companies in its bid to spread the benefits of international investment outside the major urban centres to smaller provincial towns.
- Salary packages for some Irish state company chiefs could double over the next year if the recommendations of a recent review of public sector pay is implemented.

- Booming tax revenues, up 22 per cent in the first two months of the year, are hampering Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn's effort to squeeze 40 million Irish pounds worth of cuts from cabinet colleagues to pay for the recent nurse's wage settlement.
